title: Medicaid benefits
summary: Overview of what Medicaid covers, the benefits states must offer, how benefits vary by state, and FAQs on home health care, dental care, pregnancy coverage and CHIP.

assets.alt: Father and sons on a couch

atoms.title: Medicaid eligibility by income, age or health
atoms.question: What is Medicaid health insurance for?
atoms.text: Medicaid is health insurance for people who meet certain conditions for income, age or health. This may include children, pregnant women, older adults and people with disabilities. UnitedHealthcare Community Plan's benefits page goes on to explain what Medicaid covers and how coverage varies by state.

atoms.title: Benefits every state must offer under Medicaid
atoms.question: What does Medicaid cover in all states?
atoms.text: Some Medicaid benefits are offered in all states, and the federal government gives states money for them. States must offer benefits such as family planning services, family nurse practitioner services, freestanding birth center services, health center services, home health services, inpatient and outpatient hospital services, laboratory and X-ray services, nursing facility services, pediatric care including EPSDT, physician services, pregnancy-related services, rural health clinic services, tobacco-cessation counseling for pregnant women and transportation to medical care.
questions: Does Medicaid provide transportation to appointments?

atoms.title: States can add optional benefits and cover more people
atoms.question: How do Medicaid benefits vary by state?
atoms.text: States use federal regulations to create and run Medicaid programs, and eligibility is based on income and the value of what you own. States may choose to offer more benefits and services through Medicaid, called optional benefits. They may also choose to provide coverage to larger groups of people.
questions: Why does Medicaid coverage differ between states?

atoms.title: Find Medicaid benefits for your state
atoms.question: What benefits does Medicaid cover in my state?
atoms.text: Medicaid benefits can change depending on where you live. Selecting your state on the UnitedHealthcare Community Plan site helps you find the right Community Plan to meet your health care needs and see plan details by state.
questions: How do I see my state's Medicaid benefits?
Where can I find UnitedHealthcare Community Plan benefits in my state?

atoms.title: Does Medicaid cover home health care?
atoms.question: Does Medicaid cover home health care?
atoms.text: Yes. The federal government requires all 50 states to offer some Medicaid home health care benefits. The types of home health care services offered depend on where you live. Home health services also appear on the list of benefits that states must offer.
questions: Will Medicaid pay for home health care?
Is home health required in every state's Medicaid?

atoms.title: Does Medicaid cover dental care?
atoms.question: Does Medicaid cover dental care?
atoms.text: Medicaid offers dental benefits to all youth under age 21. Adult dental coverage is optional and varies by state, so whether an adult enrollee has dental coverage depends on where they live and which benefits their state chooses to offer.
questions: Does Medicaid pay for dental work for adults?
Are children's dental services covered by Medicaid?

atoms.title: Does Medicaid cover pregnant women and babies?
atoms.question: Does Medicaid provide coverage for pregnant women and babies?
atoms.text: Medicaid covers low-income pregnant women in all states. If a pregnant woman is covered by Medicaid, their baby is too. The baby is enrolled in Medicaid for the first year of their life.
questions: Is my baby covered by Medicaid if I am?
Does Medicaid cover pregnancy in every state?

atoms.title: Does CHIP cover pregnant women and children?
atoms.question: Does CHIP cover pregnant women and children?
atoms.text: The Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) also covers pregnant women and babies in some states. CHIP may cover those who don't qualify for Medicaid. Each state offers CHIP coverage and works closely with its state Medicaid program.
questions: Can I get CHIP if I'm pregnant?
Does CHIP cover people who don't qualify for Medicaid?
